images.title: Two arcs make an eye
images.purpose: Show that an almond eye is two arcs of the same opening, with the two compass tips on opposite sides equally far from the middle.
images.composition: One large eye in the centre, one tip dot above and one below it, wide margins.
images.exact_structure: One almond-shaped eye made of an upper arc in teal #0072B2 bulging upward and a lower arc in amber #E69F00 bulging downward, meeting at 2 pointed corners left and right. One amber dot below the eye's middle (tip for the upper arc) and one teal dot above the eye's middle (tip for the lower arc), each the same distance from the middle. Faint grey #6B7280 dashed curves complete the two circles. Exactly 2 arcs and 2 tip dots.

images.takeaway: Each arc has its tip on the opposite side, equally far from the middle.
images.description: An almond eye with a teal upper arc and an amber lower arc, and two tip dots, one below and one above, equally far from the middle.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the tip for each arc and say which side it is on.

image_decisions.why: A single eye with both tips makes the idea.
